name: dusty packed wasteland earth ground, a seamless 4x4-tile field with soft tonal patches, long dry cracks and pebbles running across tile borders, mixed with tiles of shallow damp hollows
label: wasteland_ruins/dirt-b

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 96x80 seamless ground texture. Every row has the same width of 96. It has no silhouette, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no front face. Brown tonal patches, dark crack pixels, grey pebbles and darker damp hollows are scattered across the whole area. It is a flat top-down terrain tile, which suits the terrain kind, so it reads as a top-down slab with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is an earth ground field, the same kind as the grass and paving references. It has 6 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills: the whole surface carries speckle grain, soft lighter and darker patches, pebble dots and darker damp hollows. Ground has no real outline, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so they lean brown rather than black, with no sticker look. Its 6 total colours form a clear ramp from dark soil to light dust, comparable to the references' step counts. The weak point is that the long cracks are only faintly readable at this scale, and the speckle is somewhat uniform. Even so, a careful artist would accept it beside the grass reference without it looking thinner or flatter.
